\title{An improved bound on the diamond-free poset problem}

In the theory of partially-ordered sets, the two-dimensional Boolean lattice is known as the diamond. In this paper, we show that, if $\mathcal{F}$ is a family in the $n$-dimensional Boolean lattice that has no diamond as a subposet, then $|\mathcal{F}|\leq 2.206653{n\choose \lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, improving a bound by the authors and Michael Young.

The question of the size of the largest subset of the $n$-dimensional Boolean lattice, denoted $\mathcal{B}_n$, has received a great deal of recent attention from its start with Sperner's theorem in 1928~\cite{S}.  For partially-ordered sets (posets) $(\mathcal{P},\leq_{\mathcal{P}})$ and $(\mathcal{Q},\leq_{\mathcal{Q}})$, we say that a map $\varphi:\mathcal{P}\rightarrow\mathcal{Q}$ is \textit{order-preserving} if $\varphi(p_1)\leq_{\mathcal{Q}}\varphi(p_2)$ whenever $p_1\leq_{\mathcal{P}}p_2$. We say that $\mathcal{P}$ is a \textit{subposet} of $\mathcal{Q}$ if there is an injective order-preserving map from $\mathcal{P}$ to $\mathcal{Q}$ and that $\mathcal{Q}$ is \textit{$\mathcal{P}$-free} if $\mathcal{Q}$ does not contain $\mathcal{P}$ as a subposet.

Erd\H{o}s~\cite{E} generalized Sperner's theorem by finding the size of the largest $C_k$-free family in $\mathcal{B}_n$ for all values of $k$ and $n$. Exact results determining the size of the largest $\mathcal{P}$-free family in $\mathcal{B}_n$ have been found for posets, $\mathcal{P}$, known as the butterfly~\cite{DBKS} and the ``$J$'' poset~\cite{Li}. Asymptotic results have been found for the $r$-fork~\cite{KT,DBK}, the ``$N$'' poset~\cite{GK}, the height two poset $K_{r,s}$~\cite{DBK}, batons~\cite{GLu}, crowns $\mathcal{O}_{2k}$ for even $k\geq 4$~\cite{GLu} and crowns $\mathcal{O}_{2k}$ for odd $k\geq 7$~\cite{Lu}. Bukh~\cite{B} asymptotically resolved the case of posets $\mathcal{P}$ whose Hasse diagram is a tree.

Further, Griggs and Li~\cite{GLi12} classify some posets $\mathcal{P}$ as ``L-bounded''. This is not an easy condition to check but covers a number of additional cases. Each poset for which the asymptotic or exact value is known has verified the following conjecture made by Griggs and Lu:

Let $\F$ be a family in the $n$-dimensional Boolean lattice, $\mathcal{B}_n$. The quantity $n!\Lu(\F)$ counts the sum over all full chains in $\mathcal{B}_n$ of the number of incidences with the family $\F$.  For each chain that contains an $X\in\cals$ and a $Z\in\calu$, if there is some $Y\in\calt$ such that $X\subset Y\subset Z$, then assign the weight $2+\binom{|Z-X|}{|Y-X|}^{-1}$ to it.  For each chain that contains a $Y\in\calt$ but no member of $\cals\cup\calu$, then assign the weight $1$ to it.  For each chain that contains a $Y\in\calt$ and exactly one member of $\cals\cup\calu$, then assign the weight $2$ to it.  Assign the weight $13/6$ to the remaining chains.

Note that this weight assignment will upper bound $\Lu(\F)$. In fact, it will overcount chains that contain no member of $\F$ by $13/6$ and those that contain an $X\in\cals$ and a $Z\in\calu$ for which there is no $Y\in\calt$ for which $X\subset Y\subset Z$ by $1/6$.

Note that every weight is at most $13/6=2+\binom{4}{2}^{-1}$ except for those that contain an $X\in\cals$ and a $Z\in\calu$ for which a $Y\in\calt$ exists where $Y\csupset X$ or where $Y\csubset Z$. However, those are counted with the weight $2+\binom{|Z-X|}{|Y-X|}^{-1}=2+\frac{1}{|Z-X|}$.

There are a number of potential tweaks that might produce an improved result, for instance, in Remark~\ref{rem:alt} we can choose the parameters even more precisely. In that case, we were able to use Mathematica to obtain the bound $2.2066458$, without making any attempt to control roundoff error. We do note that this general method cannot obtain a bound better than $13/6$. For any family with no cover relations, the functions $f_1,g_1,\fhat_1,\ghat_1$ are all identically zero and there is no hope to obtain any improvement below $(13/6+o(1))\nntwo$ via Lemma~\ref{lem:SUbound}.
